Article Title: Watch: PM Modi inaugurates Rs 4,900 crore Chennai Metro Phase II stretch, rides train with CM Vijay
Article Text:
PM Modi took a ride on the newly inaugurated stretch with CM Joseph Vijay.

Chennai Metro services

: Timings and stations

PM Modi offers prayers

Highway, port and railway projects on agenda

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around Rs 4,900 crore.He also took a ride on the newly inaugurated stretch with Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay.PM Modi and Vijay jointly flagged off the new Metro services in the presence of Tamil Nadu Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar. The Prime Minister also purchased a ticket and briefly interacted with an employee at the ticket counter.The newly inaugurated stretch is part of Corridor 4 of Phase II and covers around 15 km, with 11 elevated Metro stations. The corridor features a unique 3.7-km double-decker structure and advanced signalling systems designed to support driverless operations.The new stretch is expected to reduce daily commuting time and improve connectivity between Chennai’s western suburbs and the city centre.According to Chennai Metro Rail, regular passenger services on the new stretch will begin at 4 pm on Sunday and operate in both directions until 9 pm.From October 12, services will run daily from 7 am to 9 pm.The last train will depart at 9 pm from both terminals: Poonamallee Bypass Metro and Vadapalani Metro on Corridor 4.The 11 stations on the new stretch are Poonamallee Bypass, Poonamallee Bus Stand, Poonamallee Government Hospital, Karayanchavadi, Kumananchavadi, Kattupakkam, Iyappanthangal, Thelliyaragaram, Porur Bypass, Porur Junction and Vadapalani.Earlier, Modi offered prayers at the Sri Jalakanteswara Swamy Temple in Tamil Nadu. He later visited the Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT Madras.The Prime Minister is also scheduled to dedicate the centre to the nation. The facility is part of a scientific initiative to map more than 100 human brains into three-dimensional atlases at cellular resolution, covering different stages of life, from the foetal stage to old age.PM Modi will also release C-STROKE, a human ischaemic stroke atlas featuring more than 1,000 annotated microscopic sections from a stroke-affected brain. The atlas is expected to help researchers identify potential new targets for treatment.Later in the day, the Prime Minister is scheduled to attend the golden jubilee celebrations of Jaigopal Garodia Hindu Vidyalaya Matriculation Higher Secondary School.During his visit, Modi will inaugurate and lay the foundation stones for National Highway projects worth around Rs 3,700 crore in Tamil Nadu.The key projects include the 36-km, four-laned Vadugapatti-Therkuvenganallur section of NH-744A, the 30-km, four-laned Madurai Ring Road section of NH-744A, and the four-lane Thiruvarur Bypass on the Nagapattinam-Thanjavur section of NH-83.He will also inaugurate five Amrit Stations at Palani, Vellore Cantonment, Ambasamudram, Paramakkudi and Namakkal.Several port-related projects at Chennai Port, Kamarajar Port and V O Chidambaranar Port are also on the agenda. These projects aim to strengthen maritime infrastructure, expand cargo-handling capacity and improve logistics efficiency.The PM will also lay the foundation stone for a Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks (LOBS) project at the existing Manali Refinery of Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited (CPCL).The project, estimated to cost around Rs 1,620 crore, will have a capacity of 270 thousand metric tonnes per annum. It aims to manufacture Group II/III lube oil base stocks for producing premium-quality lubricants in India.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project. He also took a ride on the newly inaugurated stretch with Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay. PM Modi will also lay the foundation stones for National Highway projects worth around Rs 3,700 crore.

Article Title: 'Ambani won't go out of business': Elon Musk says Starlink competition would benefit Indians
Article Text:
Musk says Starlink’s entry into India would give consumers more choices

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Sunday said that competition from Starlink would "benefit Indian consumers" by offering them more choices, arguing that Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani would not go out of business even if his profits declined.In a post on X, Musk criticised what he described as arguments made by Ambani’s supporters against Starlink’s entry into India, calling them “absurd hypocrisy and hyperbole”.“On the one hand, they say Starlink couldn’t possibly compete with the amazing low prices offered by Ambani’s de facto monopoly in India and then, in the same breath, they essentially claim that Starlink would be too strong of a competitor!” Musk wrote.“The reality is that competition would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices, as it always does. Ambani’s profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business,” he added.Musk also argued that Starlink would have to make its services affordable to attract customers. “And, obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable,” he said.Musk’s latest remarks come amid a dispute over the delay in Starlink’s commercial rollout in India. On Friday, he took a swipe at Ambani, addressing him as “Prime Minister Ambani” and alleging that he was the “real boss of India”.“Dear Prime Minister Ambani, Please accept my humble apologies for not realizing that you are the real boss of India. Naturally, you would prefer to maintain your monopolistic exploitation of the great people of India, but would you nonetheless consider allowing Starlink to compete?” Musk wrote in an earlier post.He has also alleged that unnamed business groups are trying to obstruct Starlink’s entry to protect their market positions. The government has rejected the allegations, maintaining that the delay is linked to pending regulatory and security requirements.At the India Mobile Congress 2026 in New Delhi, Union communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said India would not permit a monopoly in any sector and that three satellite communication operators had received licences: Reliance Jio Satcom, Bharti Airtel-backed Eutelsat OneWeb and Starlink.However, the government has said security clearances remain pending for the licensed operators. The satellite spectrum pricing framework is also being finalised, and commercial services can begin once the prescribed requirements are met.
Article Summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk says Starlink's entry into India would give consumers more choices. He argues that Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani would not go out of business even if his profits declined. Musk also argued that Starlink would have to make its services affordable to attract customers. His latest remarks come amid a dispute over the delay in Starlink’s commercial rollout in India.

Article Title: ‘Blatant attack on press freedom’: Journalists’ bodies condemn detention of journalists at Delhi protest
Article Text:
A protestor being dragged towards a detention bus during Jantar Mantar 2.0 on October 10 in Delhi

Reporters taken to detention centres, equipment seized

‘PIB accreditation cannot determine who can report’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Four journalists’ organisations on Saturday expressed concern over the detention of journalists covering protests in Delhi demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, saying the incident raised serious questions about press freedom.The Press Club of India (PCI), Indian Women’s Press Corps (IWPC), Delhi Union of Journalists (DUJ) and Delhi unit of the Kerala Union of Working Journalists (KUWJ) said journalists were targeted while documenting the police action. In a joint statement, they alleged that reporters carrying valid press identity cards were taken away and that some had their phones and reporting equipment confiscated, news agency PTI reported.The organisations termed the action a “blatant attack on the freedom of press” and demanded the immediate release of all detained journalists.According to the statement, journalists covering Saturday’s protests were put on buses and taken to locations including Chhatrasal Stadium and Chanakyapuri police station, alongside hundreds of protesters detained by the police.The organisations said reporters were filming the detentions when police personnel took them into custody, despite their displaying press cards. They also cited complaints that officers refused to acknowledge their journalistic credentials, with some allegedly remarking, “Everybody claims to be a journalist these days.”The statement further alleged that official reporting phones belonging to some of the detained journalists were taken away.The four bodies also objected to the Delhi Police’s reported insistence that only journalists accredited by the Press Information Bureau (PIB) could cover the protests.“Press freedom in India cannot be conditional on PIB accreditation. A large section of digital and independent media does not have PIB cards, yet they are recognised press under the law,” they said.The organisations said they had flagged the issue in a memorandum to the Delhi Police commissioner earlier in the week. However, they alleged that the concerns and recommendations raised in the representation had not been addressed.They sought an inquiry into the role of senior police officers who allegedly directed the detention of journalists even after being shown their press identification cards. Their demands also included the return of seized equipment, a public apology from Delhi Police and an assurance that reporters would be free to cover demonstrations without interference.They also said the restrictions, coupled with the detention of journalists, undermined the ability of the media to report on public protests and question institutions.“Preventing journalists from doing their job, detaining them without reason, and creating a fortress-like situation in the capital with 22,000 police and paramilitary, closed metro stations and unprecedented internet shutdowns, to stop peaceful questioning of institutions is reminiscent of a fascist state,” the statement said.
Article Summary: Four journalists’ organisations express concern over the detention of journalists covering protests in Delhi. They allege that reporters carrying valid press identity cards were taken away and that some had their phones and reporting equipment confiscated. The organisations termed the action a ‘blatant attack on the freedom of press’ and demanded the immediate release of all detained journalists.

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Nishikant Dubey on Sunday hit back at SpaceX CEO Elon Musk amid the dispute over Starlink’s entry into India, alleging that the satellite internet service poses challenges to the country’s security agencies and asserting that India would not change its security policy under pressure.In a post on X, Dubey, chairman of a parliamentary committee, said the panel had examined the challenges faced by country's security agencies in connection with Starlink.“The ministry of defence, the ministry of home affairs, and our investigation agencies are being affected by the dangerous games of these threats,” Dubey wrote.He also claimed that the government led by former prime minister Manmohan Singh had alerted the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) to such threats in 2013-14.Urging Musk to focus on making internet services affordable in the United States before criticising India, Dubey said the country was a sovereign democracy and would not alter its security policy in response to pressure or social media posts.“First, provide connections to the poor in your own country, America, at affordable rates, and then level accusations—India is a healthy democratic, sovereign nation; Article Title: 'Every Indian is angry': CJP's Ajinkya Shinde announces protests across country, starting with Mumbai's Shivaji Park at 4pm today

CJP's Ajinkya Shinde announces protests across country

NEW DELHI: New CJP leader Ajinkya Shinde has announced a protest in Mumbai against the detention of leaders and protesters across Delhi and other parts of the country, alleging that the government is clamping down on democracy.In a post on X, Shinde said protesters would assemble at T Junction in Shivaji Park at 4 pm on Sunday. He added that protests had begun across the country and more cities would join soon.“Every Indian is angry that their beloved country is being turned into a Dictatorship by Modi and Shah. The manner in which tens of thousands of people were detained yesterday across Delhi and India will not go unchallenged. Across the country protests have started against the Dictatorship,” he wrote.“The Govt has made a big mistake by arresting our leaders and clamping down on democracy. Gaddar Gyaanu Must Resign!” Shinde added.Shinde was announced as CJP’s new leader in a pre-recorded video by Abhijeet Dipke.In the video, Dipke said Shinde would lead the organisation’s protest at Jantar Mantar until he, CJP spokesperson Saurav Das and co-convener Ashutosh Ranka were released from detention. Dipke had recorded the video on Friday in anticipation of a possible arrest.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Dipke and party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das have been placed under preventive arrest and will be produced before an executive magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station on Saturday, Delhi Police said.The arrests come amid heightened security in the national capital ahead of the party’s proposed ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Mumbai local train services will be affected by megablocks on Sunday amid the CJP protest.On the Central Main Line, slow-line services between Matunga and Mulund will be diverted to the fast lines from 11.05 am to 3.55 pm.On the Harbour Line, services between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and Chunabhatti/Bandra will remain suspended on the Down line from 11.40 am to 4.40 pm and on the Up line from 11.10 am to 4.10 pm.Harbour Line passengers will be allowed to travel via the Main Line and Western Railway routes between 10 am and 6 pm.Trans-Harbour and Port Line services will operate as per schedule.
Article Summary: Mumbai local train services to be affected by megablocks amid CJP protest. Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) Dipke and party leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das have been placed under preventive arrest and will be produced before an executive magistrate at Delhi Cantt Police Station on Saturday.

Article Title: 'Interference in internal affairs': India rebukes UN human rights body over Delhi protest crackdown
Article Text:
'Extreme selectivity': India flags UN rights body's 'double standards' over Delhi crackdown (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India on Sunday rejected the UN human rights body's concerns over the security crackdown ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi, calling them “unwarranted” and an “unacceptable interference” in the country's internal affairs.In a statement, the ministry of external affairs said "India is the world’s largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary and a free media."“As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to the maintenance of public order and safety. Our law enforcement authorities act strictly in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for the redressal of any grievances,” the ministry said.The MEA also accused the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) of being selective in its public statements, alleging that it had remained silent on violent responses to protests in neighbouring countries and law enforcement actions closer to its own headquarters.“Such double standards only erode the credibility of its standing and contribute to the loss of faith in multilateralism,” the statement said.The response came a day after the UN human rights chief expressed concern over reports of mass detentions of demonstrators, protest leaders, civil society members, lawyers and journalists before and during large-scale demonstrations in Delhi.“We call on the authorities to ensure that the right to peaceful assembly is fully respected and fulfilled. Restrictions on peaceful protests must meet strict tests of necessity and proportionality,” the high commissioner for human rights said.The proposed CJP demonstration sought the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR of electoral rolls. The protest was met with a heavy security deployment and crackdown, and several political leaders and demonstrators were detained.
Article Summary: India rejects the UN human rights body's concerns over the security crackdown ahead of the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) proposed protest in Delhi. The MEA also accused the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) of being selective in its public statements.

Article Title: Personality rights: HC asks Amitabh Bachchan to appear if settlement fails
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Delhi HC has asked Amitabh Bachchan to appear in person if a settlement with several defendants in a personality rights case remains incomplete and he still wishes to pursue his claims.Justice Purushaindra K Kaurav passed the direction after the court was informed an amicable settlement had been reached with some defendants through mediation, but could not be formally signed due to logistical issues on Bachchan’s side.The court granted time to the actor to complete formalities and place the formal agreement on record. The next hearing will be on Nov 16.The HC said in the event of a non-settlement or incomplete settlement, Bachchan would have to be personally present if he wished to pursue any of his claims. His presence would enable the court to exercise its powers under provisions of Code of Civil Procedure and Section 168 of BSA, the order underlined. Section 168 empowers a judge to ask any question about any fact s/he considers necessary.
Article Summary: Delhi HC has asked Amitabh Bachchan to appear in person if a settlement with several defendants in a personality rights case remains incomplete. Justice Purushaindra K Kaurav passed the direction after the court was informed an amicable settlement had been reached with some defendants through mediation.

Article Title: 'Misplaced, unwarranted': India slams OHCHR for raising concern over SIR protest
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: India on Saturday termed the United Nations Human Rights Commission's concern over the mass detention of protesters in Delhi as "misplaced" and said the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by the country's Constitution.In a social media post on X, India at UN said the remarks by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) amounted to "unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India"."We have seen the OHCHR’s remarks about today’s events in New Delhi. India is the world’s largest democracy, where the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by our Constitution and safeguarded by robust institutions, an independent judiciary, and a free media," it said."As in every democracy, Indian citizens exercise this right subject to reasonable restrictions in the interest of public order. The authorities, for their part, act in accordance with the law, and our courts remain available to all for redressal of any grievances. The OHCHR’s concerns are therefore misplaced and constitute an unwarranted interference in the internal affairs of India," it added.It also advised the international body to "devote comparable attention" to large-scale protests in different parts of the world."In this context, OHCHR would also do well to devote comparable attention to large-scale protests elsewhere, consistent with its mandate of impartiality and non-selectivity," it said.This comes after the OHCHR raised concerns over mass detentions during the Cockroach Janata Party-led protest in New Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
Article Summary: India says the right to peaceful assembly is guaranteed by the country's Constitution. It also advised the international body to "devote comparable attention" to large-scale protests in different parts of the world. This comes after the OHCHR raised concerns over mass detentions in New Delhi.

Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

Article Title: Delhi landfill garbage mountains shrinking, 100 acres reclaimed in 18 months: CM Rekha Gupta
Article Text:
Delhi CM Rekha Gupta poses for a group picture during an on-site inspection of waste disposal operations near Okhla, in New Delhi

Government targets legacy and fresh waste

New processing plants at three sites

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

The Joe Burrow Foundation was founded in October 2022 by Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and his parents, Jimmy and Robin Burrow, to help families working to overcome food insecurity and childhood mental health issues.The foundation focuses on supporting the underprivileged and underserved, with two key areas: food insecurity and youth mental health. Article Title: From Poonamallee to Vadapalani: PM Narendra Modi launches first operational stretch of Chennai Metro Phase 2
Article Text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the first operational stretch of Chennai Metro Rail Phase-2 in Chennai





CHENNAI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the first operational stretch of Chennai Metro Rail Phase-2 connecting Poonamallee Bypass and Vadapalani by flagging off the first driverless train at Porur Bypass station.The Prime Minister purchased a paper ticket at the counter, and took a train ride from Porur Bypass station to Poonamallee Bypass station and back, accompanied by chief minister C Joseph Vijay.The 15km elevated stretch, part of Corridor-4, has 11 stations and was built at a cost of Rs 4,900 crore. It connects the western suburbs to the existing Metro network at Vadapalani, where commuters can interchange with Phase-1 services.Regular passenger services will begin at 4pm today. The services will operate until 9pm. From Monday, trains will run from 7am to 9pm, with the last services departing from both terminals at 9pm.Trains will operate every 10 minutes during peak hours — 8am to 11am and 5pm to 8pm — from Monday to Saturday, and every 15 minutes during non-peak hours. On Sundays and public holidays, services will run every 15 minutes throughout the day.The stretch includes Poonamallee Bypass, Poonamallee Bus Stand, Poonamallee Government Hospital, Karayanchavadi, Kumananchavadi, Kattupakkam, Ayyappanthangal, Thelliyagaram, Porur Bypass, Porur Junction and Vadapalani.The 3.7km double-decker section between Porur Junction and Vadapalani will not open immediately, with six stations along the stretch yet to be made operational.The new section is the first part of the 118.9km Phase-2 network, which is being developed across three corridors. The full project is expected to significantly expand Metro connectivity across Chennai.
Article Summary: The 15km elevated stretch, part of Corridor-4, has 11 stations and was built at a cost of Rs 4,900 crore. It connects the western suburbs to the existing Metro network at Vadapalani. Regular passenger services will begin at 4pm today.

Article Title: 'PERM distinct from H-1B visa': MEA on US move to suspend certain firms from green card programme
Article Text:
File photo: MEA says US move against tech firms may affect green card process, not H-1B status

Which companies have been suspended?

What is PERM, and how is it different from H-1B?

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the US government's decision to suspend several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme would not, by itself, affect existing H-1B visas or the status of visa holders and their dependents.The ministry said the suspension of applications under the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme could, however, affect the permanent residency process for eligible employees of the companies concerned.“We are aware of the US Department of Labour’s decision concerning the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme for certain companies. It should be noted that PERM is distinct from the H-1B visa programme,” the MEA said in a statement.“The suspension of PERM applications does not, by itself, affect the validity of existing H-1B visas or the status of H-1B visa holders and their dependents, though there could be some impact on the permanent-residency/Green Card process of eligible employees of the affected companies,” it added.The ministry also emphasised the economic benefits of skilled talent moving between India and the US, saying the latest measures did not advance the shared ambitions of the two countries.“It should also be clear that talent mobility adds value to both economies. While it creates opportunities for Indians, it equally helps US companies with cutting-edge talent, innovation, research, productivity, competitiveness and job creation, besides creating shareholder wealth in the US,” the MEA said.“This is therefore an area of tremendous mutual benefit for the two countries and our expectation is that all stakeholders in this process can appreciate this fact. The steps announced by the US do not advance the shared ambitions of both countries,” it added.The US department of labour has suspended Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini from the PERM programme. The department said it would not accept new applications from the affected companies or process their pending applications amid multiple active federal investigations.US labour secretary Keith Sonderling said the companies had collectively sought millions of foreign workers and received hundreds of thousands of approvals under employment-based immigration programmes.“Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They received over 230,000 H-1B visa approvals and over 100,000 permanent labour certifications. That's hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Sonderling said.The administration has alleged that companies misused employment-based immigration programmes to replace American workers with foreign employees. These are allegations made by US officials; the announcement cited ongoing investigations.PERM is a labour-certification process that allows an eligible US employer to sponsor a foreign worker for employment-based permanent residency, commonly known as a green card. Before certifying an application, the US department of labour must establish that there are not enough qualified and available American workers for the job and that employing the foreign worker would not adversely affect the wages and working conditions of similarly employed US workers.The H-1B programme, by contrast, allows US employers to hire skilled foreign workers temporarily for specialised occupations. The PERM suspension does not automatically cancel existing H-1B visas, but it could disrupt a route to permanent residency for employees whose employers are sponsoring them through the programme.The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. A day before the announcement, the US department of homeland security proposed new fees for F-1 international students seeking to participate in Optional Practical Training (OPT), describing the measure as an effort to protect American workers and strengthen the integrity of the immigration system.
Article Summary: The US government has suspended several technology companies from the employment-based green card programme. The move comes amid a wider crackdown by the Trump administration on skilled foreign labour. Microsoft, Adobe, Cognizant, Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), Wipro, HCL Technologies and Capgemini have been suspended.
