Article Title: American billionaire Mark Cuban to Americans: You are getting the 'job killer' wrong, it is not AI; it is your rising ...
Article Text:
The cost picture of US health care

What the research says

Why costs are rising

Mark Cuban's own stake

American billionaire and Shark Tank judge Mark Cuban has warned that rising healthcare costs, rather than artificial intelligence could pose a bigger threat to jobs in the United States. The founder of Cost Plus Drugs said increasing employer healthcare expenses may lead to more layoffs and reduced hiring in the years ahead. In a post shared on social media platform X (forlmekry known as Twitter) Cuban wrote, “I hope people realize that for the foreseeable future, the cost of healthcare benefits will get more people fired, or not hired, than AI." The comments come at a time when fears around AI-driven job losses continue to dominate workplace discussions. However, Cuban argued that soaring healthcare expenses are placing a greater burden on employers, forcing businesses to rethink hiring plans and workforce costs.According to a report by Fortune, the United States spends more on health care than any other country, and the total has climbed sharply. The most recent figures from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services show $5.3 trillion in spending in 2024, about 18% of GDP. That is more than double the $2.5 trillion spent in 2000. On a per-person basis, the U.S. spent $14,775 in 2024, nearly double the $7,860 spent in other high-income countries.Some studies find Americans use less care on average.Employers are feeling the squeeze. A Mercer survey of more than 1,800 employers found health care costs have risen every year for the past five years. Mercer estimates that cost per employee could rise 8.2% in 2027, the biggest jump since 2003. Nearly half of large U.S. employers, those with 500 or more employees, expect to change their medical plans next year, Mercer found. Common changes include higher deductibles or copays that raise workers' out-of-pocket costs.Part of Cuban's claim has academic support. A 2024 paper from Yale's Tobin Center for Economic Policy found that a 1% rise in health care prices leads to a roughly 0.4% drop in payroll and employment at employers outside the health sector. "Rather than cutting wages, employers respond to increases in insurance premiums by cutting the number of workers they employ," the paper said. The study measures health care prices' effect on employment. It does not compare that effect with the effect of AI, which is the comparison Cuban made. Fortune did not cite research on that point.Fortune pointed to several causes: higher labor costs, new technology and pricier treatments such as GLP-1 medications. Some experts also cite structural problems in the U.S. health care system, including hospital consolidation and rising administrative costs.Cuban is best known as a former Shark Tank investor and longtime Dallas Mavericks owner. He has become deeply involved in the health care industry since launching Cost Plus Drugs, an online discount pharmacy, in 2022.For the past four years, he has offered consumers a lower-cost route to prescription drugs. He says the company can charge less by bypassing pharmacy benefit managers. According to the nonprofit KFF, the three largest PBMs manage about 80% of prescription claims in the US. Cuban has also drawn attention to the growing health care costs that companies face.
Article Summary: Shark Tank judge Mark Cuban says rising healthcare costs may lead to more layoffs and reduced hiring in the years ahead. The comments come at a time when fears around AI-driven job losses continue to dominate workplace discussions. The United States spends more on health care than any other country, and the total has climbed sharply.

Article Title: As US government presents Science medals, Elon Musk shares 'congratulations message' for Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, Michael Dell and Satya Nadella
Article Text:
Trump honoured Elon Musk Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, Michael Dell and Satya Nadella with National Science awards (Image source: AP)

White House presents science medals

Recipients of the National Medal of Science

Elon Musk – “For engineering achievements of extraordinary ambition and scale that have pushed the frontiers of space exploration, intelligent systems, communications, and beyond, renewing American technological leadership and opening a new chapter in American manufacturing.”

Sergey Brin – “For the development of foundational algorithms for information retrieval and data processing that revolutionized how the world accesses information across science, commerce, and in the course of everyday life.”

Jensen Huang – “For advancing the graphics processing unit into a general-purpose computing architecture through innovations in processor design and software, transforming massively parallel computation and powering breakthroughs in scientific computing and super intelligence.”

Lisa Su – “For a lifetime of leadership in semiconductor engineering and high-performance computing through innovations in processor architecture and chiplet-based integration that powered the world’s first exascale supercomputer and opened new frontiers in computational performance.”

Recipients of the National Medal of Technology and Innovation

Michael Dell – “For advancing a vision of widespread adoption of personal and enterprise computing; for his technical and business management skills building a worldwide technology company; and for his support for the next generation of American scientists, engineers, and technologists.”

Satya Nadella – “For his transformative leadership of a critical American technology company, which led to its rejuvenation for a new era of cloud computing, and for his construction of the hyperscale infrastructure that enabled the training and global deployment of American super intelligence.”

US government awarded several tech executives with the country’s highest honours for scientific and technological achievements. President Donald Trump presented the National Medal of Science to Google’s co-founder Sergey Brin , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, AMD CEO Lisa Su, and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk , while the National Medal of Technology and Innovation was awarded to Dell Technologies CEO Michael Dell and Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella . Elon Musk shared a congratulatory message to fellow recipients on X.“Congratulations to Sergey, Jensen, Lisa, Michael and Satya!,” Musk wrote, replying to a video of the award ceremony event shared by the Official White House Rapid Response team.The medals were presented at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit. In a official press release, the White House said “Since 1963, the President of the United States has bestowed the National Medal of Science on those deserving of special recognition for their outstanding contributions to science in service of the United States”. White the National Medal of Technology and Innovation was first awarded in 1985. It has recognized American innovators whose vision, intellect, creativity, and determination have strengthened America’s economy and improved our quality of life.“Each of these medalists has transformed their field or industry, laying the foundations for technologies we already can barely imagine living without,” said Michael Kratsios, Assistant to the President and Director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. “While we in government work to deliver the efforts a New Golden Age of Science will require, we know that scientific progress and technological innovation depend on the insight and character of individuals. Innovators like these six awardees are the architects of the future.”The recipients are listed below.
Article Summary: US government awarded several tech executives with the country’s highest honours for scientific and technological achievements. The medals were presented at the Science: A New Golden Age Summit. Sergey Brin, Jensen Huang, Lisa Su, Michael Dell and Satya Nadella are among the recipients. Elon Musk shared a congratulatory message to fellow recipients on X.

Article Title: Michael Dell, biggest donor to Trump Accounts, defends change in rules; says: Hard for me to believe that's a bad thing, these children are going to somehow be negatively ...
Article Text:
Moving beyond low-cost index funds

Dell noted that private sector participation is picking up speed:

Michael Dell has come out strongly in defense of updated federal regulations governing Trump Accounts, dismissing warnings from skeptics who claim that permitting donors to gift individual corporate shares directly into children’s portfolios poses ethical or financial hazards. Speaking this week in an interview with Yahoo Finance, the Dell Technologies founder and billionaire philanthropist rejected allegations that such donations are part of an effort to manipulate young minds or asset markets.“It’s kind of hard for me to believe that’s a bad thing, right?” the tech titan said, adding, “That these children are going to somehow be negatively influenced because they now have one share of SpaceX , but they didn’t have before, right? The alternative is they didn’t have it, right?”“It seems unlikely that that is some kind of devious plot to somehow influence these 2 million children. If anything, they’re going to be interested in space and capitalism and how capital markets work, compounding and investing, and it will spark an interest in them that hopefully helps them as they become adults,” he added.Trump Accounts, originally authorised under last year's One Big Beautiful Tax bill, are tax-advantaged savings and investment tools structured to help children build nest eggs for retirement, college education or launching a business.Under the inaugural framework, all account contributions were required by law to sit in low-cost index funds to maximise market diversification.However, rule changes enacted last week permit charitable organisations and donors to place individual company equities into children’s accounts. So far, SpaceX president Gwynne Shotwell stands as the only major donor to commit corporate equity under the revised guidelines, promising more than 2 million shares of SpaceX stock to assist lower-income youths aged 11 to 17 living in disadvantaged communities.The policy alteration has drawn sharp criticism from financial analysts and ethicists who caution that directing children’s wealth toward single corporate entities ties their future economic baseline to an isolated business rather than broad, resilient market indices. Moreover, it has been alleged that wealthy donors could potentially orchestrate massive equity contributions to children’s funds as a means to capture tax write-offs or support corporate share prices.Michael Dell’s $6.25 billion pledge and the drive for automatic enrollmentDell and his wife, Susan, represent the single largest private donor block for the program. The couple has committed $6.25 billion to deposit $250 directly into the accounts of 25 million American children. As of October 7, more than 10 million children had received their $250 deposits, totaling $2.6 billion deployed, with the remaining balance of the full $6.25 billion pledge expected to clear by Friday (October 9).“I believe there will be a number of additional philanthropists that join us. We have now many employers that are joining in the fund here and either matching the government's contribution or going much larger and contributing to the accounts of the children that work inside their companies or even children in the communities where they operate their businesses.”The private contributions coincide with a major administrative pivot by the U.S. Department of the Treasury. On October 1, the agency transitioned Trump Accounts from a voluntary setup to automatic enrollment, establishing accounts for nearly 70 million American children under the age of 18 who hold a valid Social Security number.
Article Summary: Dell Technologies founder and billionaire philanthropist rejects allegations that such donations are part of an effort to manipulate young minds or asset markets. Trump Accounts are tax-advantaged savings and investment tools structured to help children build nest eggs for retirement, college education or launching a business.

Article Title: FPIs pull out Rs 44,166 crore from Indian equities in October so far
Article Text:
FPI withdrawals

NEW DELHI: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn Rs 44,166 crore from Indian equities so far in October, taking their total outflows in 2026 to more than Rs 3 lakh crore, as elevated crude oil prices, a stronger US dollar and high US bond yields weigh on investor sentiment.Foreign investors are also shifting funds towards North Asian markets, attracted by the rally in artificial intelligence-related stocks.The latest outflows follow net withdrawals of Rs 35,861 crore in September. FPIs had invested Rs 20,200 crore in Indian equities in July and Rs 29,631 crore in August, according to data from the National Securities Depository Ltd (NSDL).With the latest selling, FPI withdrawals from Indian equities have reached Rs 3.04 lakh crore in 2026, significantly higher than the Rs 1.66 lakh crore withdrawn during the whole of 2025, the data showed.Vedant Gupte, co-founder and CEO of investment platform Trackk, said the selling should be seen as a global shift in capital allocation rather than a negative assessment of India's investment prospects."Crude prices staying elevated on Gulf supply risk, a firmer dollar and US yields pulling money back to safer ground, and FPIs chasing the AI rally in North Asian markets where valuations currently look cheaper," he told PTI.Gupte said these factors did not point to India-specific weakness but reflected a shift towards markets where the global economic outlook appeared more favourable."We remain constructive on the medium-term outlook because domestic flows have absorbed this selling without the market cracking, which tells you the floor is sturdier than the headline outflow number suggests," he added.VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Investments Ltd, said heavy FPI selling was the primary reason for the Indian market's underperformance this year. The Nifty has delivered negative returns of 13.87% year-to-date in 2026, he said.Vijayakumar said withdrawing funds from India was a rational decision for foreign investors when the risk-free return on 10-year US government bonds was above 5.2%."So, as long as the US bond yields remain elevated, FPIs will continue to sell. The scenario will change when the valuations become attractive, and the risk-reward ratio turns favourable for investment," he said.He added that the market had been on a downward trend over the past two months, with high crude oil prices and elevated US bond yields acting as major headwinds.Foreign investors also withdrew funds from India's debt market in September. They pulled out Rs 1,921 crore through the Fully Accessible Route (FAR) and Rs 233 crore through the Voluntary Retention Route (VRR). However, they invested Rs 4,729 crore through the general route, according to the data.
Article Summary: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn Rs 44,166 crore from Indian equities so far in October. The latest outflows follow net withdrawals of Rs 35,861 crore in September. Foreign investors are also shifting funds towards North Asian markets, attracted by rally in artificial intelligence-related stocks.

Article Title: Bombay HC quashes stamp duty demands on Goregaon property transactions
Article Text:
The HC observed, “The documents have to be seen together,” and added that a stamp duty matter cannot be decided only by looking at the last document





Mumbai: The Bombay High Court has quashed stamp duty demands running into crores of rupees against firms involved in Goregaon property transactions. Authorities must consider the entire chain of documents to determine whether multiple deals formed part of a single principal transaction, rather than treating the final conveyance as a new sale, Justice Amit Borkar, sitting singly, held on Oct 5.There were four petitions that had a similar issue and the HC disposed of them by a single judgment.The petitions had challenged the legality, validity and propriety of an order dated March 3, 2016, passed by the deputy controller of stamps in Mumbai. In one of the petitions, a partnership firm, the owner of land at Laxmi Industrial Estate, Village Pahadi, Goregaon in Mumbai, said the plot was in 1977 declared to be a slum under the Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance, and Redevelopment) Act, 1971, as it was found to be encroached upon and had shanties. Landowners had entered into development-cum-sale agreements dated Dec 9, 1985, with different members of a Family for over Rs 5 lakh for five plots spread over 8,400 sq metres and the stamp duty payable was only Rs 40,000 at the time. Part of the plot was under CRZ I and part under CRZ II, also a forest area, and there were over 280 shanties. After initially getting SRA approval, in 2012, the SRA required the Petitioners to establish and complete their title in respect of the lands they had acquired development-cum-sale rights to under the Agreements of 1985 and of which they were in possession.Petitioners thus prepared four conveyances. But in 2013, the stamp authorities said the land was valued at over Rs 56 crore in 2012 and hence stamp duty payable was over Rs 2 crore. The petitioners, represented by senior counsel Aspi Chinoy, challenged such a demand. They argued the market value of 2012 could not have been applied.Vineet Naik, senior advocate appearing for the deputy controller, said the challenge was also to orders of March 2016 rejecting the appeals of the landowner, hence the stamp duty was payable.The HC said, “First question is what is the real nature of the transaction?” “According to the petitioners, the conveyances made in 2012 were only the final documents by which the transactions made in 1985, and in one case in 1996, were completed and the title was formally transferred. According to the state, the conveyances of 2012 were independent instruments. Therefore, according to the state, the market value of the properties in 2012 had to be taken. ”The HC observed, “The documents have to be seen together,” and added that a stamp duty matter cannot be decided only by looking at the last document and forgetting why and in what circumstances that document came to be made, but at the same time there should be material to show how the documents are connected.There must be some material on record showing how the different documents are connected, which Justice Borkar held was available in the case.“The long gap between the earlier agreements and the final Conveyances does not end the earlier transaction,” said the HC and held that “If the earlier agreements are read along with the possession documents, powers of attorney and receipts, and the final conveyances are seen in that background, it would not be proper to divide the transaction into one earlier transaction which had ended and another new transaction starting in 2012. The final conveyances were made to complete the transfer which had been contemplated under the earlier arrangements.”The state argued that the transactions under the earlier documents were separate and the Conveyances of 2012 must be valued independently. “I am unable to accept this submission. The material shows continuity in the parties, continuity in the properties and continuity in the rights…” Justice Borkar said.The petition has also said the 2012 ready reckoner could not have been applied as the properties were affected by various restrictions, including slum conditions, CRZ or environmental restrictions, mangroves, reservations, road reservations and other development restrictions. The HC said that while the RR forms the starting point, in every case it cannot prove the true market value and the state had to factor in the circumstances of the particular properties. The HC said, however, since the 2012 conveyance was held not to be a fresh one but to be the final document completing the 1985 sale, it didn’t need to decide on the RR aspect.The HC held, “Authorities treated the Conveyances of 2012 as if an entirely new sale had taken place in 2012 and thereafter applied the market value of 2012 to that fresh transaction. The material on record does not support this basic factual assumption,” and set aside the stamp duty demand in crores based on the 2012 market price.
Article Summary: The Bombay High Court quashed stamp duty demands running into crores of rupees against firms involved in Goregaon property transactions. Authorities must consider the entire chain of documents to determine whether multiple deals formed part of a single principal transaction, the court said.

Article Title: BJP’s Kirit Somaiya questions actor Imran Khan’s citizenship
Article Text:
Mumbai:

TOI





Actor Imran Khan ’s participation in the August Kranti Maidan protest has stirred up a controversy with BJP politician Kirit Somaiya questioning how a foreign citizen can participate in a protest in India. Somaiya, in a post on X, said he has written to the joint commissioner of police, Manoj Kumar Sharma , seeking action against Khan for participating in the protest despite being a foreign citizen.tried to reach Khan following Somaiya’s post, but he was not available for comment.Imran Khan, speaking to the media moments before being detained, said, “I am here as a citizen, as a person who lives in this city. I am here to see why freedom of movement is being restricted, why are people’s voices being repressed.”Civil rights activist and senior counsel Mihir Desai said a foreigner would not have the same “fundamental right” under the Indian Constitution to protest in India against Indian policies, but he would have a “restricted right to protest”. He cited Article 19 of Indian Constitution which gives a fundamental right to assemble and free speech to citizens of India.
Article Summary: BJP politician Kirit Somaiya questions how a foreign citizen can participate in a protest in India. Khan was not available for comment. Civil rights activist and senior counsel Mihir Desai said a foreigner would not have the same “fundamental right” under the Indian Constitution to protest.

Article Title: 50%+ of respondents from IIT Bombay Class of 2026 from large cities, metros: Survey
Article Text:
IIT-B

Mumbai:





More than 50% of IIT Bombay ’s graduating students who responded to an annual survey conducted by the institute’s student media body, Insight, hail from large (32.6%) and metropolitan (20.8%) cities. Meanwhile, 37.5% of the respondents said they came from smaller cities or towns, while only 9% reported coming from villages. Among the survey’s interesting findings, more than 85% of respondents said their parents had completed undergraduate or postgraduate education in either STEM or non-STEM fields.While Insight conducts the senior survey among graduating students every year, only around 144 of the 2,400 students in the graduating batch of 2026 responded.The Senior Survey 2026 explored a wide range of aspects of campus life, including students’ demographics, academic performance, career plans, lifestyle and social experiences. The survey covered everything from satisfaction with grades and placement outcomes to mental health, personal growth on campus, parents’ educational backgrounds and even dietary preferences.In response to a question about violating the institute’s honour code, a large majority of respondents said they had never cheated on assignments or exams.However, nearly a quarter admitted to having cheated ‘once or twice out of desperation’, including some students with higher cumulative performance indices (CPIs).Insight, in a disclaimer, claimed that the findings presented in the survey may not entirely reflect the views and experiences of the whole graduating student body, while students called it a ‘leisure’ survey.On the subject of branch changes, one-fourth of the respondents said they would have opted for computer science and engineering if given the opportunity to change their branch. In a separate question, 32.4% of respondents said better placement opportunities would motivate their decision to switch branches.When asked whether they had sought counselling or therapy while on campus, 41 students said they had never felt the need for it, while 33 said they had managed their difficulties with support from friends and family. Meanwhile, 24 respondents said they had used the institute’s counselling services, while 25 said they had wanted to seek counselling but had never taken the first step.Around 32% of respondents said they were unsure whether they would remain in the same field over the next five years, while 28% said they already had an exit plan. Additionally, 21% said they would have preferred to pursue higher studies or research after graduating from IIT Bombay if money were never a factor.
Article Summary: More than 50% of IIT Bombay’s graduating students hail from large (32.6%) and metropolitan (20.8%) cities. 37.5% of the respondents said they came from smaller cities or towns, while only 9% reported coming from villages. 85% of respondents said their parents had completed undergraduate or postgraduate education.

Article Title: Central Railway’s ‘Swachhata Rath’ Removes 1.68 Lakh Kg Muck to Ensure Clean Tracks
Article Text:
Mumbai:





Central Railway’s (CR) dedicated Muck Special train—popularly known as the “Swachhata Rath”—cleared an impressive 1.68 lakh kg of garbage, waste and muck in a single focused drive along the CSMT–Dadar section, an official announced on Saturday.Operating during a designated four-hour Muck special block, the initiative deployed 881 personnel, including trackmen, sanitation workers, supervisors and contractual staff. The specialised clean-up targeted key vulnerable spots across CSMT, Masjid, Parel, Dadar and Matunga stations. The 1.68 lakh kg of muck was packed into 2,800 gunny bags.CR chief spokesperson Swapnil Nila emphasised that while CR remains committed to maintaining a clean environment, public cooperation is essential. Central Railway appeals to all commuters to refrain from throwing garbage on railway tracks.
Article Summary: Central Railway’s dedicated Muck Special train cleared 1.68 lakh kg of garbage, waste and muck in a single focused drive along the CSMT–Dadar section. The specialised clean-up targeted key vulnerable spots across CSMT, Masjid, Parel, Dadar and Matunga stations.

Article Title: Where did last year’s Rs 3,000-crore relief package go, Danve asks govt
Article Text:
State govt has yet to clarify the status of the pending assistance or announce a timeline for disbursing fresh aid to the drought-affected farmers

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Shiv Sena (UBT) MLC Ambadas Danve on Friday slammed BJP-led Mahayuti govt over the alleged non-disbursal of financial aid to drought-hit farmers, questioning the fate of the Rs 3,000-crore relief package announced last year, of which nearly Rs 500 crore in dues allegedly remained unpaid.Raising the issue amid mounting agrarian distress, Danve accused govt of making lofty announcements without ensuring that relief actually reached farmers on the ground. “Govt had announced a Rs 3,000 crore package last year. Where did that package go? Around Rs 500 crore from last year is still pending. This is the question we are raising,” Danve said.The MLC also sought clarity on the assistance planned for farmers affected by the ongoing drought, saying while govt had identified drought-hit talukas, it had yet to spell out the nature or timeline of financial support. “Govt has announced the number of drought-affected talukas. It should now tell farmers what assistance it intends to provide and when,” he said.Danve took a swipe at govt’s handling of the agrarian crisis and said farmers continued to suffer severe financial stress. “Farmers are dying by suicide every day. Such is the grim situation they are facing,” he said.Backing the criticism, All India Kisan Sabha president Rajaj Kshirsagar alleged that farmers reeling from repeated crop losses had been denied timely compensation and support.“Farmers facing successive agricultural setbacks have been seeking timely compensation and financial support to manage mounting losses. But govt is least concerned about the farmers, who are ending their lives unable to bear the stress,” Kshirsagar said.Congress city district president Syed Akram echoed the opposition’s concerns, saying the core issue was the widening gap between govt assurances and the actual delivery of relief. “Danve’s criticism reflects the concerns raised by all opposition parties. We are demanding accountability for pending dues and a clear commitment on fresh relief for farmers,” Akram said.
Article Summary: BJP-led Mahayuti govt slammed over alleged non-disbursal of financial aid to drought-hit farmers. MLC Ambadas Danve questioned fate of Rs 3,000-crore relief package announced last year. Nearly Rs 500 crore in dues allegedly remained unpaid.

Article Title: Upset over unpaid salary, former staffer of cash management firm plots ATM hard disk thefts, held
Article Text:
Investigators said the firm never filed a police complaint in any of the thefts, despite the missing devices containing crucial CCTV footage

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





What allegedly began as a disgruntled employee’s attempt to recover three months’ unpaid wages has exposed an ATM surveillance equipment theft racket, with Parbhani police arresting a former cash management services (CMS) technician and his associates on Thursday on charges of stealing hard disks from at least 27 ATM kiosks across Maharashtra Investigators said the firm never filed a police complaint in any of the thefts, despite the missing devices containing crucial CCTV footage.According to police, Vishal Dhaktode(20) of Mukundwadi in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar had worked as a CCTV technician with the cash management firm responsible for maintaining ATM surveillance systems. “Dhaktode quit his job earlier this year after his employer allegedly withheld three months of salary. Frustrated over repeated failed attempts to recover his dues, he removed hard disks from three public sector bank ATM kiosks and refused to return them till he was paid,” police said.The strategy apparently worked. Police said the firm eventually cleared his pending salary and recovered the stolen hard disks, purportedly choosing a quiet settlement over legal action to avoid reputational damage and potential scrutiny from the bank.But what started as an act of retaliation allegedly snowballed into a larger operation. “During the investigation, we found that the gang had allegedly stolen 27 hard disks. What is particularly concerning is that the firm had not registered an FIR in any of these incidents, despite the thefts involving equipment containing CCTV footage,” Parbhani superintendent of police Pankaj Kumawat said.While the theft of a hard disk does not affect ATM operations or customer transactions, it effectively erases stored surveillance footage, potentially hampering investigations into crimes committed at the kiosks.The wider racket came to light during a probe into the theft of hard disks from three public sector bank’s ATMs in Parbhani city in the early hours of Thursday. The targeted kiosks were located near Bhikulal Petrol Pump, Kanti Chowk and Mahatma Phule Colony on Super Market Road.A joint team of local crime branch (LCB) and Nanapeth police nabbed Sachin Uday Yadav (23) and Prafull Shankar Sonawane (22) of Jalna within hours of receiving information about the thefts. Investigators then traced and Dhaktode in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.LCB inspector Gajendra Sarode said coordinated police action led to rapid breakthroughs in the case. “We acted swiftly after receiving information about the three ATM thefts in Parbhani. Two suspects were detained within two hours, and our team subsequently apprehended the third accused in Sambhajinagar,” he said.Nanapeth police have registered a case under relevant provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections 331(4), 305, 62 and 3(5) and seized three 4TB hard disks, a motorcycle, two cellphones, two screwdrivers and a black bag from the accused. The total value of the seized property is estimated at Rs 3.02 lakh.Investigators are now probing the full extent of the alleged network and examining why repeated thefts of sensitive ATM surveillance equipment failed to trigger any formal complaint from the company entrusted with securing them.
Article Summary: Police arrest former cash management services (CMS) technician and his associates on charges of stealing hard disks from at least 27 ATM kiosks across Maharashtra. Investigators said the firm never filed a police complaint in any of the thefts, despite the missing devices containing crucial CCTV footage.

Article Title: ​​GMCH irregularities: Probe panel summons health activists
Article Text:
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The state inquiry into alleged irregularities at Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar has moved to the next stage, with health activists and former members of the board of visitors summoned to appear before the probe committee on Friday.The four-member panel, headed by Dr Sushil Deshmukh, dean of GMCH, Nanded, has directed Pravin Shinde and Iqbal Singh Gill to appear in person with documents and submissions related to complaints filed through the state’s ‘Aaple Sarkar’ grievance portal.On Oct 3, the panel members visited GMCH, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, to retrieve bills, work orders, and rate comparison charts, among other details concerning the alleged irregularities, corruption, and inflated procurement. However, during that visit, the panel did not officially record the complainants’ testimonies, forcing them to lodge fresh complaints on the ‘Aaple Sarkar’ portal.The inquiry panel has been mandated to investigate the sanctioning of 27 ‘small constructions’ worth around Rs50 crore—allegedly executed without proper authorisation—the purchase of drugs and machinery at inflated rates, and a Rs33 lakh expenditure recorded for a 30-minute in-house event.These matters revolve around Dr Shivaji Sukre, who holds the additional charge as dean of GMCH and is currently under scrutiny.Several insiders from the hospital have called for a rigorous investigation by the panel. “The reputation and image of GMCH have suffered like never before, eroding the faith of underprivileged patients. The inquiry must be fair and speedy, and panel members must not succumb to any pressure or allurements,” a senior doctor from GMCH said on the condition of anonymity.The hearing will be held at the regional office of the Directorate of Medical Education and Research ( DMER ) in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.Dr Syeda Afroz Fatima, dean of GMCH, Jalna, serves as the member secretary of the panel. Its other members include Dr Prakash Gattani, head of the pharmacology department at GMCH, Jalna, and JS Lakhade, administrative officer at DMER, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.
Article Summary: The inquiry panel has been mandated to investigate the sanctioning of 27 ‘small constructions’ worth around Rs50 crore. The purchase of drugs and machinery at inflated rates, and a Rs33 lakh expenditure recorded for a 30-minute in-house event.

Article Title: Raju Shetti demands Rs5,000/tonne initial payout for sugar cane farmers
Article Text:
Kolhapur





: Farmers’ leader and former MP Raju Shetti on Saturday demanded an initial payment of Rs5,000 per tonne for sugar cane for the upcoming crushing season, warning that farmers will prevent mills from starting operations if this demand is not met.Addressing the Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana’s (SSS) 25th sugar cane conference in Kolhapur, Shetti said soaring production costs and severe drought have worsened the financial difficulties faced by farmers.“Sugar cane to be crushed this season must receive a first instalment of Rs5,000 per tonne. Production costs have skyrocketed, and sugar cane farmers are in deep trouble due to the drought. In such a situation, farmers must get a fair price for their hard work. Sugar factories must announce this initial payout; otherwise, we will not allow them to start the crushing season,” Shetti warned.He further cautioned that the organisation will indefinitely block national highway traffic at the Kognoli toll booth on the Maharashtra–Karnataka border on October 13 if a favourable decision is not reached during the central government’s scheduled meeting on Oct 12.Additionally, Shetti demanded that the central and state govts provide sugarane growers a subsidy of Rs500 per tonne to compensate for harvesting delays and reduced sugar recovery during transit.He argued that cane harvested after Dec 15 should receive an extra Rs300 per tonne above the fixed rate.Citing widespread crop failures and the acute distress faced by farmers and livestock due to insufficient rainfall, the SSS leader demanded that the state govt deposit drought assistance of Rs1 lakh per hectare directly into the bank accounts of affected farmers. He also sought an increase in the incentive for regular loan repayments under the Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Loan Waiver Scheme, urging it to be raised from Rs50,000 to Rs1 lakh.Turning his focus to industry transparency, Shetti alleged rampant irregularities in weighing, sugar recovery metrics, and stock transactions at sugar mills. He demanded that every factory’s weighing scale be digitised and linked to a transparent online system.He noted that declining ethanol production would heavily burden sugar factories with high interest and instalments on project loans, which would ultimately hurt sugarcane farmers. To mitigate this, he sought a full-year interest subsidy and extended repayment schedules for ethanol project loans.Highlighting that five crore sugar cane farmers and 1.5 lakh workers and agricultural labourers depend entirely on the industry, Shetti demanded a special financial stability policy. He also urged the government to facilitate loans for private and cooperative sugar factories at a concessional 4% annual interest rate through NABARD, the Sugar Development Fund, or the National Cooperative Development Corporation.
Article Summary: Raju Shetti is the leader of Swabhimani Shetkari Sanghatana (SSS) The organisation is holding its 25th sugar cane conference in Kolhapur. Shetti said soaring production costs and severe drought have worsened the financial difficulties faced by farmers.

Article Title: Almost 100% crop loss seen, blanket compensation on the cards: Agriculture minister Bharne
Article Text:
Bharne with local MLA Babasaheb Deshmukh inspected crop damage in Sangola taluka of Solapur district

Kolhapur:





State agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne on Friday said crop loss assessment of over 1 crore hectares of kharif plantation has been completed and there is 100% loss in the drought-hit talukas. The compensation will thus not be partial but a blanket one, he added while speaking to the media after visiting fields in Sangola taluka of Solapur district.The minister said crop loss assessment has been completed on around 67% of total kharif plantations in the state. “In the next four days, the crop loss assessment of entire 1.49 cr hectares of area under kharif cultivation will be completed. There is no such thing as partial loss; there is 100% loss of the crops in drought hit talukas and therefore compensation will not be partial but a blanket one.”Bharne assured that the farmers will be compensated for crop loss before Diwali. “First, the compensation as per NDRF guidelines will be given to the farmers. Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis has assured maximum compensation as possible,” he said, stating that out of eight agricultural divisions, Amravati division is leading with 91% coverage of crop loss assessment, followed by Latur with 84%, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar with 70%, Pune with 58%, Nagpur with 48%, Nashik with 39%, Kolhapur with 29% and Konkan with 17%.The state has declared drought in 265 talukas and has now given directions to local authorities to carry out crop loss assessment in 18 additional talukas, as the local MLAs there have complained about severe water scarcity and crop damage.Bharne said that govt has released Rs 13,500 cr to waive the loans of the farmers with loan dues less than Rs 2 lakh; there are 30 lakh such farmers. “There are around 3 lakh farmers with loan amount more than Rs 2 lakh; the farmers will have to settle the amount over and above Rs 2 lakh. The third list of beneficiaries will be those who have paid the loans regularly; there are 22 lakh such farmers. Owing to some KYC issues and bank queries, the list got delayed, but soon, these farmers will also get the incentive promised as per Ahilyadevi Shetkari Karjmafi Yojana,” said Bharne.
Article Summary: State agriculture minister Dattatray Bharne on Friday said crop loss assessment of over 1 crore hectares of kharif plantation has been completed. The compensation will thus not be partial but a blanket one, he added while speaking to the media after visiting fields in Sangola taluka of Solapur district.

Article Title: Bananas soaked in ethephon? 1,394kg stock seized in Navi Mumbai raid after video triggers alarm
Article Text:
The inspection revealed that bananas were treated with BTHILEX, which is prohibited for direct use on fruit (Visuals credit: X)





NAVI MUMBAI: Acting on a tip-off, a food safety officer with panch witnesses inspected a stall at APMC Fruit Market, Turbhe, and allegedly found a worker artificially ripening bananas by dipping them in BTHILEX, labelled Ethephon 39% soluble liquid, a plant growth regulator.Officials said the seller claimed he mixed two caps of the chemical in five litres of water.The team seized 1,394kg of bananas, worth about Rs 67,814, stored for sale under Section 38 of the Food Safety and Standards Act , 2006.Three statutory samples of bananas and a surveillance sample of the chemical solution were collected for analysis.Officials said the BTHILEX packaging carried apparently illegitimate manufacturer details, including address, pin code and contact number, and lacked a Central Insecticides Board and Registration Committee registration number.FDA officials said the product may be counterfeit or unregistered and is being referred for action under the Insecticides Act, 1968.They said ethephon can only be used to generate ethylene gas; dipping fruit directly in it is prohibited because residues may pose human health risks.
Article Summary: Food safety officer seized 1,394kg of bananas, worth about Rs 67,814. BTHILEX, a plant growth regulator, can only be used to generate ethylene gas. Dipping fruit directly in it is prohibited because residues may pose human health risks.

Article Title: Navi Mumbai Police destroy 726kg narcotics worth Rs 26.30 crore; 3,200 arrested in 5 years
Article Text:
Navi Mumbai police destroyed 726 kgs of narcotics valued at Rs 26.30 crore through incineration





NAVI MUMBAI: Navi Mumbai Police destroyed 726 kg of narcotics worth Rs 26.30 crore that were seized from arrested drug peddlers and suppliers in 201 cases under the NDPS (Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances) Act, 1985, registered at various police stations.The contraband was destroyed on Wednesday at the incineration plant of the government-approved Mumbai Waste Management Company in Taloja, following the legal process and obtaining a court order.Accordingly, till date, the city police have destroyed seized narcotics worth a total of Rs 139.74 crore in 393 NDPS Act cases.In the past five years, police have seized 1,078 kg of narcotics worth around Rs 150 crore and arrested 3,200 accused in 2,378 NDPS Act cases, informed senior inspector Sandeep Nigade of the Anti-Narcotics Cell.SI Nigade said, "In June, the Navi Mumbai police destroyed narcotics collectively worth Rs 56.69 crore that was seized in 26 cases registered under NDPS Act. In March, narcotics collectively worth Rs 18.63 crore that was seized in 55 cases was destroyed. While, in Feb last year, we had destroyed Rs 10 crore worth narcotics seized in 40 drugs peddling cases of contrabands including charas, ganja, MD, MDMA and LSD, which were registered under NDPS Act in 2023 and 2024.Thereafter, Rs 38.45 crore worth drugs seized in 114 cases was destroyed in Sept last year."DCP (Crime) Sachin Gunjal informed, "From 2023 till 2025, a total of 1529 accused African nationals arrested for drugs peddling in the city have been deported and 911 accused African nationals have been blacklisted in the Navi Mumbai Police Commissionerate for illegally staying and selling narcotics. Maharashtra Control of Organized Crime Act (MOCCA) has been invoked against the accused found repeatedly indulging in drugs trafficking. "Police commissioner Milind Bharambe said, "To make the anti-drugs operation more effective and faster at the local level, a separate 'Anti Narcotics Squad' has been set up at every police station in Navi Mumbai Police Commissionerate.The squad has been assigned the responsibility of collecting local information about drugs peddling, strengthen the network of informants, regular patrolling and inspection at schools, colleges, hotels, lodges, pubs, bars and crime sensitive areas.Also, monitoring of newly emerging drug trends and taking immediate action, scientific investigation and filing of chargesheet in cases registered under NDPS Act.Extensive public awareness programs are being organized in schools, colleges, housing societies and public places. Helpline number '8828-112-112' has already been launched for the citizens to provide any information about drugs peddling and the caller's is kept confidential."
Article Summary: The contraband was destroyed on Wednesday at the incineration plant of the government-approved Mumbai Waste Management Company in Taloja. Till date, the city police have destroyed seized narcotics worth a total of Rs 139.74 crore in 393 NDPS Act cases.

Article Title: Young scientists map Murbad biodiversity amid project row
Article Text:
A group of young scientists is diligently conducting biodiversity surveys to underscore the environmental importance of the area. (Photo credit: Joeanna Fernandes)

Each field visit costs Rs 15,000–20,000, funded largely through donations. (Photo credit: Joeanna Fernandes)

Conflicting assessments

Volunteers believe their data will help challenge what they see as gaps in official impact assessments. (Photo credit: Joeanna Fernandes)

A learning exchange

Two projects and a movement

Kalu Dam:

Location: Kalu river, Murbad taluka, Thane district

Benefits: Dam will supply 1140 MLD to Mumbai region’s cities

Impacts: 2,258.86 ha of land and 18,000 people in Murbad, Thane

Pumped Storage Project

What: A PSP is a type of large-scale water battery that stores and releases electricity on demand, using water and gravity.

Location: Thane and Pune district

Benefits: Supply 1500 MW energy

Impacts: 166.05 ha of land and 2,653 people, company says no one will be displaced

Wildlife impact:

Species count from draft EIA: 273 plants; 27 birds; 14 reptiles; 3 amphibians

Species count on iNaturalist: 468 plants, 154 birds, 34 reptiles; 13 amphibians

Kalu Dam Timeline:

1993: Chitale Committee recommends dam at Kalu

2009: Kalu Dam formally announced

2011: Shramik Mukti Sanghatana files PIL against dam in Bombay HC

2012: HC issues stay on construction work; environment ministry’s forest committee rejects clearance for dam

2013: New forest committee sets aside previous verdict, recommends in-principle clearance

2016: ACB books five engineers from KIDC and partners of FA Enterprises, given work of dam, on charges of cheating and fraud related to the dam.

2020: HC lifts stay, allowing construction to resume

2026: Land acquisition process initiated

2013: New forest committee sets aside previous verdict, recommends in-principal clearance

2016: Five engineers from KIDC and partners of FA Enterprises, booked on charges of cheating and fraudrelated to dam

2020: HC lifts stay

2026: Land acquisition initiated





MURBAD/THANE: Near midnight on a recent Friday, a dozen young men were herded into a pickup truck parked outside Titwala railway station.Around 55 km away, in a bamboo shed doubling as a tribal museum and community centre, a blue tarpaulin awaited them on the earthen floor—their bed for the weekend.Many of the men were strangers to each other, and to Vaishakhare, a village in Murbad where two projects are planned within 10-12 km of each other: the Kalu Dam and the Malshej Ghat Bhorande Pumped Storage Project (PSP), an energy storage plant.Both projects have been opposed by locals who fear displacement or loss of livelihood.The dam, to be built by the Konkan Irrigation Development Corporation (KIDC) and funded by the Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), will supply drinking water to Thane, Bhiwandi, Ambernath, and other cities.It is expected to acquire 2,258.86 hectares and impact an estimated 18,000 people. Meanwhile, the 1500 MW PSP, to be built by Adani Renewable Energy Fifty Two Limited, will acquire 166.05 ha and impact at least three villages.Local opposition has recently gained an unlikely ally: young city scientists.For the past year, 20-something botanists, zoologists, and biologists from colleges in Thane, Pune, and Mumbai, have been descending on Kalu and Bhorande, site of the PSP's lower reservoir, to conduct biodiversity surveys and document the community’s ties to the landscape.The aim is to build research-backed evidence of the area’s environmental and cultural significance.“There is no baseline data on the Kalu river and only the People’s Biodiversity Register for Bhorande forest. We need studies robust enough to hold up in court,” says wildlife conservationist Avinash Harad.Initially, they had invited senior scientists to conduct surveys, but their requirements were too costly, he says. So the organisations backing the movement — Shramik Mukti Sanghatana and Ashwamedh Prathisthan—turned to young scientists willing to sleep on a tarp.Each field visit costs Rs 15,000–20,000, funded largely through donations.To date, some 70 researchers have done fieldwork in Murbad, and another 30 have analysed data remotely.“We don't need complex equipment or labs. For most biodiversity studies, photographic evidence is enough,” says Jehu Nadar, a 26-year-old zoologist. He and others hope to publish at least 20 research papers in the coming years.Researchers are not simply counting species but documenting the ties binding people to place: the local Thakar, Mahadeo-Koli and Katkari adivasis — the last classified as a ‘Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group’ — hold traditional rights to forest resources.Volunteers believe their data will help challenge what they see as gaps in official impact assessments.Their data has already thrown up a discrepancy. Around 1,419 species have been logged in the area so far, including 468 plant, 154 bird, 34 reptile and 13 amphibian species.This is more than double the number documented in the draft Environment Impact Assessment (EIA) for the storage project, published this May.Nadar flagged another issue: the 26 fish species listed in the draft EIA were attributed to a 2016 study at an entirely different Kalu Dam in Ahilyanagar (Ahmednagar), more than 100 km from here. (The Murbad dam is exempt from an EIA because it is a drinking water project.)In an email response to TOI, a spokesperson for the Adani Group rejected the allegations, saying: "Project assessments indicate no anticipated impact on local flora, fauna, livelihoods, communities or nearby cultural and tourism sites.”The company says it is committed to “environmental safeguards and continued engagement with local communities, while contributing to local infrastructure, livelihoods and regional development."There are also differing claims about people. The draft EIA mentions 2,653 affected people, but the company says this refers simply to the population of the 10-sq-km study area, not the project site.While the project will affect three villages, it will not displace anyone, says the company. However, at least 15 villages have been served public hearing notices by the state pollution control board, says Harad.Nine of them, including Bhorande, have passed resolutions opposing the project.Meanwhile, the gram sabha process for the dam is underway, says Sudarshan Pagar, Executive Director, KIDC, Thane.The land acquisition proposal has been submitted to the district collector's office and the required resolutions will be obtained as per statutory provisions, including PESA, he added.Currently, data on affected houses and families is being collected, Pagar says. Once finalised, a rehabilitation plan will be prepared and submitted to the Divisional Commissioner, Konkan Division, he adds.For some volunteers, the fieldwork has been sobering. "I didn't realise the gravity of the situation until I came here," says Rajas Shrikoli, 24, a marine biologist who signed up expecting a fun excursion.Scientists may be new to the movement, but young people have long been part of it, says Indavi Tulpule, an activist and legal advocate who has led the Kalu agitation for decades. When the dam was first announced in 2009, students from TISS Tuljapur, Nirmala Niketan and colleges in Kalyan helped collect data on potential impacts. Tulpule hopes to deploy research data for any legal battles that might arise. But there are also intangible benefits to the scientific effort.Harad says the presence of city researchers has spurred local youth to engage more deeply with their landscape, potentially opening up work as environmental and cultural guides.The knowledge exchange has run both ways. Under a karanda tree in Bhorande forest, Daulat Pardhi, 29, a guide from the Thakar community, points out a plant curled like a shepherd's crook on the ground, called Gulabdani for its pink flower.When the flowers dry and fall, Pardhi grinds them into powder and uses it to heal wounds. “My mother taught me this,” he says.
Article Summary: The Kalu Dam and the Malshej Ghat Bhorande Pumped Storage Project (PSP) are planned within 10-12 km of each other. Both projects have been opposed by locals who fear displacement or loss of livelihood. Local opposition has recently gained an unlikely ally: young city scientists. They are conducting biodiversity surveys to underscore the environmental importance of the area.

Article Title: At 35.9°C, city logs hottest Oct day in 22 years
Article Text:
IMD data showed that the day’s maximum temperature at Shivajinagar was 4° above normal

Pune:





Shivajinagar on Saturday logged a maximum temperature of 35.9°C, making it the city’s hottest Oct day since 2003. The last time temperature was highest during the month was on Oct 7, 2002, when the station recorded 36.9°C.According to weather experts from Vagaries of Weather blog, Saturday’s reading is the highest October maximum recorded at Shivajinagar since the 2002 peak.Data from India Meteorological Department (IMD) showed that the day’s maximum temperature at Shivajinagar was 4° above normal. Elevated temperatures were recorded across the district, indicating a widespread heat surge.Among other monitoring stations, Wadgaon Sheri recorded 35.5°C, followed by Baramati and NDA at 35.4°C each. Talegaon registered 35.3°C, while Hadapsar recorded 34.8°C. Temperatures at Pashan-AWS, Chinchwad, and Magarpatta stood at 34.5°C, 34.4°C and 34°C, respectively.The unusually high Oct temperatures have pushed daytime conditions well above seasonal averages, marking one of the warmest spells the city has experienced in recent years.
Article Summary: Shivajinagar on Saturday logged a maximum temperature of 35.9°C, making it the city’s hottest Oct day since 2003. The last time temperature was highest during the month was on Oct 7, 2002. Elevated temperatures were recorded across the district, indicating a widespread heat surge.

Article Title: Solapur farmer, 2 aides cheat trustee of ₹87L on ₹50cr loan promise
Article Text:
Indian currency notes of different values

Pune:





Narhe police arrested a farmer from Solapur district for allegedly duping a 65-year-old trustee of an educational trust of ₹87 lakh by promising a ₹50 crore low-interest loan between Dec 2023 and June.When the trustee, whose trust runs educational institutes in the Narhe and Sinhagad Road areas, demanded his money back after the loan failed to materialise, the suspects handed him bags claiming that they had cash.However, when he opened the bags, he found old bedsheets, newspapers and bricks. The trustee then lodged a complaint with the police on Friday.Varsha Deshmukh, senior inspector of Narhe police station, said, “We have arrested Anup Divekar (42) of Solapur. Earlier, he used to stay in Nigdi Pradhikaran. Divekar and his two accomplices had met the trustee through a common friend in 2023.”According to the FIR, the trustee was looking for a loan at lower interest rates because the trust had bought an educational campus in the city and it was running at a loss. The trustee needed funds to develop it and make it more attractive to students. While looking for a loan, he came in contact with the three suspects through a common friend.“The three suspects claimed that they had good contacts with financial institutions and could arrange a loan for the trustee at lower interest rates,” Deshmukh said.“The suspects allegedly demanded a 10% commission to arrange the Rs 50 crore loan. They gave the trustee fake documents and asked him to pay them in cash, through bank transfers from the accounts of employees of the educational campuses, and through online transfers. In all, the trustee paid them Rs 87 lakh towards their fees, loan processing charges and other expenses,” Deshmukh said.“After receiving the money, the suspects allegedly gave the trustee some cheques, which bounced one after the other. They first gave Rs 50 crore in cheques, which all bounced. Subsequently, they gave Rs 25 crore, Rs 5 crore and Rs 10 crore in cheques. They also bounced," she said.“After the cheques were dishonoured, the trustee demanded his Rs 87 lakh back. The suspects then handed him bags filled with old bedsheets, bricks and old newspapers,” Deshmukh said.
Article Summary: Anup Divekar, 42, of Solapur, was arrested for allegedly duping a 65-year-old trustee. Divekar and his two accomplices met the trustee through a common friend in 2023. The suspects allegedly demanded a 10% commission to arrange the Rs 50 crore loan. They allegedly gave the trustee some cheques, which bounced one after the other.
